events.title: The Sea Peoples Attack
events.description: Groups of sea peoples attack the coasts around the eastern Mediterranean. Egypt manages to repel them under Ramses III, but many other empires fall.

events.title: The Philistines Settle Down
events.description: The Philistines, likely part of the sea peoples, settle along the southern coast of Canaan and establish five city-states: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron, and Gath.

events.title: The Iron Age Begins
events.description: Iron gradually replaces bronze as the dominant material for tools and weapons. The fall of the Hittites spreads iron technology to new peoples.

events.title: Egypt's Decline
events.description: After Ramses III, Egypt gradually weakens. The New Kingdom ends, and Egypt is split between priests in Thebes and pharaohs in Tanis.

events.title: The Rise of the Phoenicians
events.description: The city-states of Tyre, Sidon, and Byblos survive the collapse of the Bronze Age and become leading maritime and trading powers in the Mediterranean.

events.title: The Phoenician Alphabet
events.description: The Phoenicians develop an alphabet with 22 letters that becomes the precursor to the Greek, Latin, and Hebrew alphabets.

events.title: Aramean Kingdoms
events.description: Aramean tribes establish kingdoms in Syria, including Damascus. Aramaic gradually becomes the lingua franca throughout the Middle East.

events.title: Tiglath-Pileser I of Assyria
events.description: The Assyrian king Tiglath-Pileser I temporarily expands Assyrian power westward to the Mediterranean, but the empire weakens after his death.

events.title: The Greek Dark Ages
events.description: After the fall of the Mycenaean civilization, Greece enters a period of population decline, loss of writing, and reduced trade.

events.title: The Zhou Dynasty in China
events.description: The Zhou dynasty takes power from the Shang and introduces the 'Mandate of Heaven' as justification for royal authority. The longest dynasty in Chinese history.
